implementation.scope: Scientific prose only; original support statuses preserved; Reschke full-text gap remains

claims.bg_proposition: Somogyi 1959, Diabetogenic Effect of Hyperinsulinism, 26:192-198 is the source for the specific 1959 clinical excess-insulin rebound case account.

source_checks.author_year: Somogyi 1959, Exacerbation of Diabetes by Excess Insulin Action
source_checks.region: title, case-study framing, and night-to-next-day glycosuria interpretation

claims.correction_proposal: Cite 26:169-191, PMID 13617275 for this specific 1959 case account; distinguish 26:192-198, PMID 13617276, and do not call either the first publication of the hypothesis.

claims.bg_proposition: A CGM low below 3.5 mmol/L followed by morning hyperglycaemia identifies a Somogyi pattern.

source_checks.region: Table 1 including group denominators and morning glucose means, methods continued from p.1
source_checks.context: 594 valid nights in 89 selected T1D participants; confirmed nocturnal low <=2.2 mmol/L for >=10 min; morning glucose 6.1 +/- 0.3 vs 11.5 +/- 0.2 mmol/L; means +/- SEM
Selected CGM cohort n=88; 23% of morning hyperglycaemia cases had nocturnal hypoglycaemia; no hormone or treatment attribution

claims.correction_proposal: Call the trace a post-hypoglycaemic rise; reserve Somogyi for a proposed hormonal mechanism and state CGM alone cannot identify the cause.

claims.bg_proposition: There is a definite intrinsic 24-hour tissue-coordinated insulin-sensitivity curve with a T1D morning trough.

source_checks.region: Methods, circadian-phase, misalignment and behavioural-cycle SI results
source_checks.context: 14 healthy adults; no significant intrinsic circadian-phase SI effect (p=0.06); behavioural dinner SI -25.4%; misalignment SI -16.5% (95% CI 7.9-24.3)

claims.correction_proposal: Separate endogenous phase, behavioural meal timing and misalignment; label T1D tissue-resolved phase/amplitude unestablished.

claims.bg_proposition: Harfmann 2016 shows abolished diurnal muscle glucose uptake and glucose intolerance with normal insulin secretion.

source_checks.region: glucose-tolerance methods and Figure 2 with caption
source_checks.context: Mouse glucose tolerance tested at ZT14; approximately 2-fold higher fasting insulin concentration in muscle-Bmal1 knockout; insulin secretion rate not measured

claims.correction_proposal: Limit Harfmann attribution to measured mouse endpoints; check Dyar 2014 independently before attributing a rhythm-abolition or normal secretion claim.

claims.bg_proposition: Seven Widom deteriorators showed a 19% luteal decline in glucose disposal.

source_checks.context: Seven participants selected by prior premenstrual hyperglycaemia history; 30.2 +/- 3.8 vs 24.5 +/- 2.0 umol/kg/min, p=0.09; Figure 1 mean +/- SE; hyperglycaemic clamp 11.7 mmol/L

claims.correction_proposal: State p=0.09 and preselection next to the effect size; do not infer phenotype prevalence from seven of sixteen.

claims.bg_proposition: Scheer 2009 isolates circadian misalignment with adequate or constant sleep and produces a 6% postprandial glucose rise.

source_checks.region: Effects of Circadian Misalignment results and sleep-efficiency comparison
source_checks.context: Ten healthy adults; glucose +6% and insulin +22% averaged across behavioural cycle; sleep efficiency 67% vs 84%, n=9 sleep records

claims.correction_proposal: Retain observational estimates with their whole-cycle endpoint; remove adequate-sleep and independent-of-sleep claims from Scheer attribution.

claims.bg_proposition: Van Cauter 1991 shows glucose +17% and calculated insulin secretion +49% under nocturnal wakefulness.

source_checks.region: Table I and clearance Results text
source_checks.context: Eight healthy men on continuous IV glucose; mean +/- SEM nocturnal-wakefulness rises 16.6 +/- 4.7% glucose and 49.3 +/- 7.6% secretion; clearance 1.57 +/- 0.20 L/min 23:00-03:00 vs 1.16 +/- 0.13 L/min 08:00-11:00, p<0.01

claims.correction_proposal: Add the measured secretion-versus-circulating-insulin distinction and clearance timing; do not treat it as T1D subcutaneous-insulin calibration.

claims.bg_proposition: BG attributes the SWEET seasonality paper to Kamrath et al. 2022 and uses it, with a T1D-incidence Mendelian-randomization null finding, to infer infection and vitamin D contributions to seasonal HbA1c in established T1D.

source_checks.context: Genetic vitamin D exposure versus T1D incidence risk, not HbA1c in established T1D

source_checks.locator: primary indexed abstract and bibliographic title
source_checks.context: Seasonality of new-onset paediatric T1D cases and first-year HbA1c, not seasonal HbA1c nadir in established T1D

claims.correction_proposal: Correct author attribution to Reschke et al. 2022; remove cross-endpoint inference or replace with endpoint-matched longitudinal/intervention data. Full Reschke paper not independently appraised.
